method: 8 frames at 1,3,…,15 s; must-haves of V2/bench/mcp/flower/items/I94a.json; flower-judge (effort medium) per film; flower-pair (effort medium), random order; the same judge keyref-1 and keyref2 were scored with

mcp.summary: A warm, visually polished ad follows the requested story and ends on the correctly branded shop front, but dawn is only suggested and the opening sign misspells the brand.

must_haves.item: The florist opens the shop at dawn, arranges a bouquet, and hands it to a smiling customer at the door, in that order.
must_haves.why: Opening the door, arranging the bouquet and handing it to a smiling customer appear in order; the golden light suggests early morning but does not clearly establish dawn.

must_haves.item: The florist, the customer and the bouquet stay the same throughout; no extra or floating bouquets.
must_haves.why: The florist and customer appear consistent, and the pink-and-white bouquet retains its brown wrapping; no unexplained duplicate or floating bouquet is visible.
Warm sunlight illuminates the storefront, people and flowers consistently.

must_haves.item: It ends on the shop front, with the name reading exactly "Petal & Stem" if a sign is shown.
must_haves.why: The final frame shows the shop front with the exact text "Petal & Stem", although the opening sign incorrectly reads "Peal & Sten".
The supplied timestamps span the stated 16-second ad, and all frames are widescreen 16:9.

v3-flower-1.summary: An attractive, warmly lit ad with correct branding and a strong shop-front ending, but it omits clear bouquet arranging and undermines the handoff by leaving the bouquet with the florist.

must_haves.item: The florist opens the shop at dawn, arranges a bouquet, and hands it to a smiling customer at the door, in that order.
must_haves.why: The door opens in low, early-day-looking light, and a smiling customer reaches for the bouquet at the doorway; however, the florist already holds a finished bouquet, no arranging is shown, and the transfer does not clearly complete.

must_haves.item: The florist, the customer and the bouquet stay the same throughout; no extra or floating bouquets.
must_haves.why: The people and main bouquet look broadly consistent, with no obvious floating duplicate, but bouquet possession reverses: the customer grasps it at 7–9 seconds, yet the florist holds it again at 11–15 seconds.
Soft, low-angle daylight gives the wooden storefront and people a warm, natural appearance, supplemented by interior lamps.

must_haves.item: It ends on the shop front, with the name reading exactly "Petal & Stem" if a sign is shown.
must_haves.why: The final frame is a wide view of the shop front, and the sign clearly reads "Petal & Stem".
The supplied frames are 16:9 and span 1–15 seconds, consistent with the stated 16-second runtime.

v3-flower-1 vs mcp.why: The second video more clearly follows the required opening–arranging–handoff sequence, keeps the bouquet with the smiling customer after the exchange, and ends on a warmly lit shop front with the correct “Petal & Stem” name. Its opening sign is misspelled, but the first video largely skips bouquet arrangement and repeatedly returns the bouquet to the florist after the apparent handoff, making it less faithful overall.
